query: how to triage your inbox with ai
title: How to triage your inbox with AI | 50agents
description: Triage your inbox with AI: sort unread mail into reply, read, file and ignore, draft the replies, and never let it delete, unsubscribe or send without you.
h1: How to triage your inbox with AI
answer: Have an AI read your unread email at set times, sort each message into four piles (needs a reply, needs reading, file it, ignore it), draft replies for the first pile, and leave everything in your inbox for you to send or archive.
Start with labels and drafts only; letting AI delete, unsubscribe or send on its own is where triage goes wrong.

body.p: Four piles, not twelve. Every extra category is a decision the AI can get wrong and you have to check.

sections.h2: What Gmail and Outlook already do

head: Gemini in Gmail
Copilot in Outlook
rows: "Prioritize my inbox": high, normal or low, with a reason
Google says all Workspace plans, and Gmail users on a Google AI plan
Its Chat needs a business Microsoft Copilot subscription and a work or school account
Runs on its own on a schedule

body.p: Both are good when you are already in the inbox. What they do not do is go through your mail at 8:00 before you arrive and have the drafts waiting. That is the job for an AI agent or an automation with an AI step.
Google’s own help warns that Gemini may suggest inaccurate information. Treat every draft from any tool as a draft.

method.h2: How to set it up, step by step

steps.title: Write your four piles in one line each
steps.body: "Reply: a client or supplier asking me something. Read: reports and team updates. File: receipts and invoices. Ignore: newsletters."

steps.title: Pick the times
steps.body: Once before you start (8:00) and once after lunch is plenty. Every few minutes costs more and interrupts more.

steps.title: Give it your voice and facts
steps.body: Three sentences on how you write, your sign-off, and the facts it will need (prices, hours, links). Without them, drafts sound like nobody.

steps.title: Start with labels and drafts only
steps.body: No archiving, deleting, unsubscribing or sending. You stay the one who moves mail out of the inbox.

steps.title: Read the first week’s piles
steps.body: Look for anything important in Ignore. Fix the one-line rules until nothing important is misfiled for a week.

body: In 50agents this is one sentence to Captain. It builds an AI agent that goes through your unread email now, then every weekday at 8:00, and drafts the replies. It marks handled mail so the next run skips it, says what it searched for when it finds nothing, and asks you before any email leaves.

wrong.title: An invoice in Ignore
wrong.body: A rule like "ignore anything automated" catches bills. Name what must never be ignored: invoices, contracts, anything from your bank.

wrong.title: Auto-archive hides mail
wrong.body: You never see what was archived. Keep everything in the inbox with labels until you trust the rules.

wrong.title: Unsubscribed from something you needed
wrong.body: Do not let AI unsubscribe for you. Review the Ignore pile and unsubscribe yourself.

wrong.title: Encrypted or shared mailboxes skipped
wrong.body: Copilot cannot read S/MIME or Double Key Encryption mail, and shared and group mailboxes have limits, according to Microsoft’s FAQ. Other tools have similar gaps; check yours.

wrong.title: "No unread email" when there was
wrong.body: The tool searched for the word "unread" instead of using the unread state. Ask it to say what it searched for.

faqs.q: Can AI manage my inbox for me?
faqs.a: It can sort, summarise and draft. Keep sending, deleting and unsubscribing for yourself, at least until its drafts and labels are right week after week.

faqs.q: Does Gmail have AI sorting built in?
faqs.a: Gmail has its own categories and filters, and Gemini can summarise and draft. Neither runs a scheduled pass that drafts replies before you open your inbox.

faqs.q: Is it safe to give AI access to my email?
faqs.a: Limit what it may do: read, label, draft. Every send should wait for you. Read the vendor’s data terms before connecting.
